text:
Elliot Price: Quick IA review for the Quickstart Templates landing pages before I ask Design to lock layout (DES-147). Draft nav + sections here: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts (preview)

Elliot Price: Main questions:
1) Where does “Production checklist” live? Top-level page vs per-template.
2) Copy: do we say “Quickstart templates” everywhere or just “templates”?

Wei Chen: Skimmed. +1 on consistency: use “Quickstart templates” as the noun, “template” when referring to a specific one.

Wei Chen: On checklist: I’d prefer top-level *and* a short “You’re in production mode” callout on each template page. If it’s only top-level, people skip it. If it’s only per-template, it gets repetitive.

Renee Sullivan: +1. The support-agent reference app page is going to link directly to the RAG+agent template, not the landing page. If checklist is only on landing page, it won’t be seen.

Elliot Price: Makes sense. I was worried about page length, but a compact callout could work.

Marissa Cole: From Console/rollouts POV: the checklist should show up *before* “Deploy” instructions. Otherwise folks ship the defaults to prod and then ask why logs are noisy / missing request_id. Maybe a callout block right after “Run locally”.

Kira Thompson: Also please add a small “Dedicated/Private note” callout somewhere. Not a full guide, but at least “If you need data isolation / VPC, see …” with link to the Dedicated/Private section.

Wei Chen: Copy nit: on landing page you say “Production-ready in 15 minutes” in the hero. That reads like a promise. Maybe “First successful run in ~15 minutes” + “Production shape from day one” lower down.

Elliot Price: Good catch. I’ll tone that down.

Alex Martinez: +1 to “production shape” language. We should avoid implying “secure for prod by default” without caveats. But we *can* be confident about guardrails: timeouts, retries/backoff, structured logs, OTel wiring.

Elliot Price: On placement proposal:
- Landing page: keep a “Production checklist” section with 8–10 bullets and links to deeper pages.
- Each template page: add a “Before you deploy” callout w/ top 4 items + link to the full checklist.

Renee Sullivan: Works. For the callout bullets: include “Set REDWOOD_REQUEST_ID / correlation ID propagation” (whatever we’re calling it) because every demo question turns into “how do I find this in Console.”

Wei Chen: Re: terms, can we standardize the sections as:
- Choose a template (RAG / Agents / RAG+Agents)
- Run locally
- Add observability (traces/logs/metrics)
- Deploy
- Production checklist
Then per-template pages can follow the same skeleton.

Marissa Cole: On “Add observability” section: please mention “Observability pack” explicitly + what it includes (dashboards + alert rules) and link to import instructions. People don’t know what “pack” means.

Elliot Price: Yep. I’ll add one sentence: “Includes dashboards for latency p95, token cost, error rate by class, 429s/timeouts.”

Kira Thompson: Another wording tweak: avoid “on-prem” in the hero. It’s a footnote for most readers. Maybe put Hosted first, then Dedicated, then Private. Something like “Works with Hosted now, scales to Dedicated/Private when you need isolation or residency.”

Wei Chen: +1. Also on landing page you have “Agents (tool calling)” and “RAG (vector DB)”. I’d rename to “Agents (tool calling)” and “RAG (retrieval + citations)” — vector DB is implementation detail.

Renee Sullivan: +1 to “citations” language. Developers care about “where did it come from” more than “we used pgvector.”

Elliot Price: Noted.

Wei Chen: Small IA thing: where do we put “Production checklist” in the left nav? If it’s buried under each template, it’s harder to find. I suggest a top-level “Production checklist” page under Quickstarts, and per-template pages just link to it.

Elliot Price: Agree. Left nav: Quickstarts -> Overview, Templates (3 pages), Production checklist, Observability setup.

Marissa Cole: Another nit: “Observability setup” vs “Add observability” — pick one term. Setup reads like “install these 12 things.” Maybe “Observability (OTel + dashboards)”.

Alex Martinez: Re checklist content: make sure we include:
- Set timeouts (don’t rely on SDK defaults)
- Retries/backoff + 429 handling
- PII/logging guidance (no raw prompts in INFO)
- Tool allow-list + tool timeouts
This is the stuff that turns into tickets.

Elliot Price: Got it. I’ll pull bullets from the safe-defaults checklist.

Wei Chen: Can we add a sentence near the top: “These are templates, not a framework.” There’s always one thread asking “do you support X tool plugin.”

Elliot Price: Yep. I’ll add under “What you get.”

Elliot Price: Action items:
- [Elliot] Update landing hero copy + rename RAG label + add observability pack sentence.
- [Wei] Propose final nav order + per-template skeleton headings.
- [Kira] Send me the exact Dedicated/Private callout text + link target.
- [Marissa] Sanity check the “before you deploy” callout bullets for Console alignment.

Renee Sullivan: I’ll also review for “demo flow” readability once you push the edits.

Elliot Price: Cool. I’ll post updated preview link later today.
